name: Marisol Lane
home: the western blocks near Ferry Street Rooms
life: “I still remember finding my own reflection in another family's wedding album.” Monday often includes a stop at Studio Boulevard, where Marisol waits by the window where the whole crossing can be seen without leaning into the road.
voice: I don't remember my wedding outfit. The salon owner found me reflected in another bride's photograph.
appearance: Marisol is easy to recognize by silver temples and a dark fringe and a long face and high cheekbones. Usually dressed in a rust-colored canvas coat with a printed handkerchief folded into the pocket, Marisol squares up pieces of paper while thinking when listening.
personality: Marisol finds names easy and faces hard on a crowded street. People who assume they have been snubbed usually get a warmer greeting once they speak.
agenda: To take home a photograph of the forgotten wedding outfit.
family: Elias Lau is Marisol’s younger relative by marriage. Marisol leaves the first voice message. Elias calls back when there is finally a little privacy. In their family a missed ring can mean a bus, a customer, a sleeping child or a bad hour. Neither treats it as an answer in itself. Asked about *The million-dollar flat*, Elias says, “I own the identical flat downstairs and owe the bank more than anyone imagines.”
connections: Avery Lai. A new interview and an old wedding both turn up unexpectedly in reflections.

reactions.situation: A client asks to sit outside the shared mirror's view
reactions.response: Marisol puts the person's chair outside the reflection and lets them choose when to look.

reactions.situation: A cyclist goes down in a crowded crossing
reactions.response: Marisol stays with the rider after the people who saw the fall start drifting away.

reactions.situation: When somebody waves from across traffic
reactions.response: Marisol waits at the corner to hear their voice and give them a proper answer.
